style_prefix: Photorealistic candid photo on an Indian construction site, documentary style, natural daylight, realistic PPE and equipment detail.
style_suffix: Clean composition, single clear subject, no text, no captions, no watermarks, no arrows, no icons, no illustration elements.

2.A: A simple narrow leather waist belt with a metal buckle lying on a wooden site table, construction tools in background — a plain single waist belt only, no shoulder or leg straps.
2.B: An Indian construction worker wearing a complete full-body safety harness with shoulder straps, chest strap, thigh straps and a steel dorsal D-ring on the upper back, standing on site, front three-quarter view.
2.C: An Indian construction worker with a thick rough manila rope tied in a crude knot around his chest over his shirt, standing on a construction site — improvised and unsafe.
2.D: A wide black leather gym weightlifting belt with velcro and buckle lying on a site bench — a gym accessory, clearly not fall-protection equipment.

4.A: Close-up of ordinary thin prescription reading glasses with slim frames on an Indian worker's face, orange grinding sparks flying nearby, the small lenses clearly leaving the sides of the eyes exposed.
4.B: An Indian worker wearing sealed chemical-splash safety goggles plus a clear polycarbonate full face shield over them, bright grinder sparks bouncing harmlessly off the shield.
4.C: An Indian worker wearing dark fashion sunglasses on a construction site while orange sparks from an angle grinder fly around his unprotected face.
4.D: An Indian worker grinding steel with an angle grinder with completely bare eyes, no eyewear at all, squinting as bright sparks fly directly toward his face.

9.A: Close-up of a full-body safety harness worn by an Indian worker, front view, showing a steel D-ring mounted on the front chest strap at sternum level.
9.B: Rear view close-up of a full-body safety harness on an Indian worker, showing the steel dorsal D-ring positioned on the upper back between the shoulder blades with a lanyard clipped to it.
9.C: Side view of a full-body safety harness on an Indian worker showing a steel D-ring mounted at the side of the hip on the waist belt.
9.D: An Indian construction worker's white hard hat with a steel D-ring absurdly bolted to the very top of the helmet shell, close-up.

10.A: A long aluminium extension ladder leaning against a tall brick wall at a very shallow flat angle of about 45 degrees, its base pulled far away from the wall, on a construction site.
10.B: A long aluminium extension ladder leaning against a tall brick wall at the correct steep climbing angle of about 75 degrees, base one quarter of the height away from the wall, an Indian worker holding the base steady.
10.C: A long aluminium extension ladder standing almost perfectly vertical, pressed flat at 90 degrees against a tall brick wall, looking unstable and about to tip backward.
10.D: An aluminium extension ladder carelessly thrown against a wall at an awkward crooked sideways angle, one foot off the ground, clearly placed with no measurement at all.

11.A: A scaffold working platform with a proper steel top guardrail at waist height (about 1 metre above the deck) plus a midrail and toe board, an Indian worker standing safely behind it.
11.B: A scaffold working platform edge with only a tiny steel rail running at ankle height, an Indian worker standing beside it, the open drop clearly visible above the useless low rail.
11.C: A scaffold working platform with a completely open unguarded edge, no guardrail at all, an Indian worker standing near the exposed drop.
11.D: A scaffold platform edge with only a single thin sagging nylon rope stretched loosely between posts as the only barrier, clearly flimsy.

18.A: A scaffold platform edge fitted with a decorative painted wooden trim strip in bright festival colours, purely cosmetic, on an Indian construction site.
18.B: Close-up of a scaffold platform edge with a proper timber toe board along the deck edge, a steel wrench resting against the inside of the board which stops it sliding off the edge.
18.C: An Indian worker climbing the outside of a scaffold gripping the low timber toe board at platform-edge level like a handhold, clearly misusing it.
18.D: A scaffold platform where several timber toe boards are stacked flat on top of each other in the middle of the deck like height-boosting blocks, a worker about to step on the unstable stack.

21.A: An Indian worker climbing a ladder awkwardly with a heavy power drill clutched in one hand, only one hand gripping the rung, body off balance.
21.B: An Indian worker climbing a ladder correctly with both hands on the side rails, his hammer, screwdrivers and spanners neatly secured in a leather tool belt pouch at his waist.
21.C: One Indian worker at the bottom of a ladder throwing a hammer up through the air toward a second worker who leans off the ladder trying to catch it.
21.D: An Indian worker climbing a ladder with a long screwdriver clenched between his teeth, both this dangerous and absurd, close view of his strained face.

22.A: An Indian worker holding an angle grinder, carefully comparing the new cutting disc against the tool before fitting, the metal wheel guard properly mounted on the grinder.
22.B: An Indian worker forcing an oversized cutting disc that is too large onto a small angle grinder spindle, the disc overhanging badly, no guard fitted.
22.C: Low angle photo of an Indian worker's feet wearing open rubber sandals right next to a running angle grinder on the ground, sparks flying near his exposed toes.
22.D: An angle grinder being used with its wheel guard removed completely, the spinning disc fully exposed, stream of orange sparks flying straight at the operator.

23.A: An Indian maintenance worker using a compressed-air nozzle to blow dust and metal shavings out of an open machine housing, debris flying away from him.
23.B: An Indian worker pointing a compressed-air gun directly at a co-worker's dusty shirt and bare forearm at close range, dust blasting off the clothing onto skin — dangerous misuse.
23.C: An Indian worker inflating a large truck tyre with an air hose while watching the pressure gauge in his other hand.
23.D: A pneumatic nail gun connected to a coiled yellow air hose being used normally by an Indian worker on timber formwork.

24.A: Three cheap thin extension cords plugged into each other end-to-end in a long daisy chain, connectors lying in mud across an Indian construction site.
24.B: A single heavy-duty industrial yellow extension cord, neatly routed and elevated off the ground on insulated hooks along a dry wall, powering one tool, inspection tag on the plug.
24.C: An orange extension cord with its joint connector lying submerged in a muddy rainwater puddle on a construction site, still plugged in.
24.D: A flimsy thin white household two-pin extension cord powering a huge heavy-duty concrete cutting saw on a construction site, cord visibly too light for the machine.

28.A: A brass padlock locking the hasp of a corrugated steel storage shed door on a construction site, tools visible through the gap.
28.B: Close-up of an electrical isolator switch on an industrial panel locked in the OFF position with a red safety padlock and a bright red-and-white danger tag hanging from it, maintenance tools nearby.
28.C: A handwritten name label tied with string to the handle of a steel toolbox on a site workbench.
28.D: A heavy chain and padlock securing the main steel entrance gate of a construction site at dusk, site boards visible.

32.A: A black electrical cable stretched tight across a busy construction site walkway at ankle height, workers' boots about to catch on it — obvious trip hazard.
32.B: Temporary site power cables routed neatly overhead on tall yellow insulated stands above a walkway, completely clear of foot traffic, dry ground below.
32.C: An electrical power cable running directly through a long muddy rainwater puddle on a construction site, half submerged.
32.D: A long electrical cable left loosely coiled in sticky wet mud near a site entrance, connectors buried in the dirt.

33.A: A steel scaffold standard (vertical leg) sinking and tilting into loose soft excavated soil with no support plate, visibly unstable.
33.B: A steel scaffold leg standing on a square steel base plate centred on a solid timber mud sill board, on firm level ground — textbook correct footing.
33.C: A steel scaffold leg balanced on a wobbly stack of loose red bricks, bricks misaligned, clearly makeshift and dangerous.
33.D: A steel scaffold leg propped on random construction debris — broken concrete chunks and a bent metal sheet — on uneven ground.

36.A: A scaffold working platform with wide open gaps between scattered planks, the drop to the ground visible through the gaps.
36.B: A scaffold working platform fully decked with tight-fitting timber planks edge to edge, no gaps, secured with couplers, an Indian worker standing on it confidently.
36.C: A scaffold platform with planks covering only one half of the frame, the other half completely open bare steel tubes.
36.D: Loose unsecured scaffold planks sliding apart under an Indian worker's boot as he steps on them, planks skewed at angles.

40.A: A wide excavation trench on an Indian site with both walls cut back at a gentle safe slope angle, benched steps of soil, workers visible at the bottom.
40.B: A trench with vertical walls supported by hydraulic aluminium shoring struts braced between both faces at regular intervals.
40.C: A deep trench with a heavy steel trench box shield installed, workers working safely inside the protected steel enclosure.
40.D: An Indian worker standing at the bottom of a deep trench pressing his bare hands flat against the raw earth wall as if holding it up — absurd and extremely unsafe.

43.A: A row of exposed vertical steel rebar ends protruding from a concrete foundation, tips bare, sharp and rusty at waist height — impalement hazard.
43.B: A row of vertical steel rebar ends each fitted with a bright orange plastic mushroom safety cap, neat and uniform on an Indian construction site.
43.C: A row of rebar ends where only two or three bars are crudely bent over sideways and the rest still stand sharp and exposed.
43.D: Vertical rebar ends wrapped with a few thin loose turns of red-white striped warning tape only, sharp tips still visible through the tape.

52.A: A yellow ventilated steel flammable-liquids storage cabinet with louvred vents standing in an open shaded area of a construction site, far from any work activity, LPG cylinders chained upright beside it.
52.B: Red diesel jerry cans and an LPG cylinder stacked directly beside an active welding station with bright sparks showering over them — extremely dangerous.
52.C: Petrol cans and paint thinner bottles stored inside a cramped site office cabin right next to a glowing electric room heater.
52.D: Fuel drums and solvent cans dumped unorganised in a dark unventilated storeroom corner, one drum leaking onto the floor.

53.A: Indian workers calmly walking down a wide concrete emergency exit staircase in single file during a site evacuation drill, green exit signage visible above.
53.B: A construction site material hoist / elevator with its doors standing open, smoke haze in the air, completely empty as evacuating workers walk past it toward the stairs.
53.C: A group of Indian construction workers gathered in orderly rows at an open-air assembly area on site, supervisor counting heads on a clipboard.
53.D: An Indian worker's hand pulling down the lever of a red wall-mounted fire alarm call point on a site wall.

54.A: A crane lifting a bundle of steel beams high overhead while the ground area directly beneath is cordoned off with red-and-white barrier tape and cones, all workers standing well outside the zone.
54.B: An Indian worker sprinting directly underneath a large concrete block suspended from a crane hook, load hanging right above his head.
54.C: A crane operator leaning from his cab window waving a worker to walk through underneath the suspended load above.
54.D: An Indian worker standing calmly directly below a huge suspended steel load, pointing at his yellow hard hat as if it protects him.

58.A: An Indian worker lifting a heavy cement bag correctly: knees deeply bent, back straight and upright, bag held close against his torso, squatting form.
58.B: An Indian worker lifting a heavy cement bag dangerously: legs locked straight, bending fully at the waist, back rounded, the bag held far out in front at arm's length.
58.C: An Indian worker mid-lift twisting his upper body sharply sideways while holding a heavy box, spine visibly rotated under load.
58.D: An Indian worker trying to lift a heavy sack with one hand while his other hand holds a mobile phone to his ear.

61.A: An Indian construction worker standing on open high ground taking a deep breath of clean fresh morning air, arms relaxed, clear sky.
61.B: An Indian worker wading bare-legged through stagnant muddy floodwater in a waterlogged trench, a rat visible on debris near the water's edge.
61.C: An Indian worker neatly dressed in full PPE — gloves, gumboots, helmet and hi-vis vest — standing on a dry construction site.
61.D: An Indian worker drinking clean water from a clear sealed bottle during a site break, water visibly clean.

62.A: Indian office staff working at computers in a clean air-conditioned site office cabin, dry and tidy.
62.B: Indian workers digging in a deep waterlogged excavation trench, standing in muddy stagnant water with shovels, drainage pipes visible.
62.C: An Indian truck driver sitting in the dry cab of a tipper truck on a construction site, window down.
62.D: Visitors in clean clothes and white visitor helmets being escorted along a dry walkway at the edge of a construction site.

68.A: An Indian technician safely repairing a switched-off machine placed on a workbench, tools laid out neatly, machine clearly powered down.
68.B: An Indian worker standing directly in the path of a large reversing dump truck on site, the truck bearing down behind him as he faces away.
68.C: An Indian worker standing at a safe distance to the side of a welding hot-work area, sparks contained behind a welding screen.
68.D: An Indian worker on a quiet dry site walking without helmet or vest, no machinery anywhere near him.

69.A: A pair of brown steel-toe safety shoes alone on the edge of a high concrete slab, nothing else — footwear only.
69.B: An Indian worker at height on a steel structure wearing a full-body harness with BOTH lanyard hooks clipped to a steel lifeline above — 100 percent tie-off.
69.C: A pair of grey cotton work gloves lying alone on a high steel beam, nothing else.
69.D: A single orange reflective safety vest hanging alone on a scaffold pole at height, nothing else.
